title: API + Orchestrator + Adapter Ownership: proposal and boundaries
content:
Purpose
- Short: propose a clean, low-friction split of responsibilities across API gateway, central orchestration (control plane), and runtime adapters. Aim for easy owner boundaries, clear SLOs, and minimal cross-team change blast radius when we evolve routing policies or add new hardware adapters.

Goals and constraints
- Goals: enable independent deploy/ownership cycles for gateway, orchestrator, and adapters; support multi-region failover and region-affinity; make routing policies expressible and testable; keep per-tenant isolation options simple to opt in.
- Constraints: single control plane config store (git-backed + leader reconcile) for consistency; runtime adapters must be lightweight network services with stable HTTP/gRPC contracts; regional routing must avoid cross-region tokenization of secrets.

High-level proposal (one-line)
- API gateway owns request ingress, auth enforcement, and primary routing decision at request start.
- Orchestration/control plane owns global routing policies, rollout/traffic-split decisions, model/version metadata, and policy distribution to gateways/adapters.
- Runtime adapters own the translation between control-plane model metadata and the concrete runtime (GPU pools, quantized blobs, provider hooks) and expose a standard runtime capability interface.

Service responsibilities (detailed)
- API Gateway (team: platform-gateway)
  - Responsibilities: TLS, customer auth (tokens), rate-limit enforcement, per-tenant quota accounting, initial policy lookup, sticky headers for session affinity, short-circuit fallbacks for throttled tenants.
  - Bounded responsibilities: does NOT own model version lifecycle, does not modify model metadata, does not manage GPU pools.
  - Surface contract: routes requests to orchestrator-route endpoint with {tenant, routeHints, selector} and expects route decision (routeId, adapterEndpoint, modelId, sessionHeaders).

- Control Plane / Orchestrator (team: platform-orchestration)
  - Responsibilities: canonical policy store (git + reconciler), canary/rollout APIs, global and regional routing policies, weight-based traffic shaping, model catalog (versions, compatibility), region capacity awareness, policy delta notifications.
  - Bounded responsibilities: does NOT proxy request traffic (no data plane payload relay), does not hold long-lived secrets used by adapters (KMS handles secret distribution).
  - Surface contract: accepts route evaluation queries (lightweight) and emits signed route decisions and push updates to gateways and adapters via webhook/stream.

- Runtime Adapters (team: serving-runtime and infra-adapters)
  - Responsibilities: map modelId -> runtime artifact, manage local cache of model shards/quantized artifacts, expose inference endpoints, report health/metrics, perform admission checks (model compatibility, memory checks).
  - Adapter types (proposal):
    - hardware-adapter (NVIDIA, A100/T4)
    - cpu-optimized-adapter (x86 quantized paths)
    - cloud-provider-adapter (GCP/Azure native integrations)
    - simulator-adapter (for testing, cheap dev)
  - Bounded responsibilities: adapters should not make global routing decisions; they can suggest local fallbacks (e.g., degrade model quality) but must always accept signed route decisions from orchestrator/gateway.
  - Surface contract: gRPC inference API + health + model-manifest sync endpoint. Manifest schema v1 is the single expected shape.

Routing policy taxonomy (expressible in orchestrator)
- Latency first (latency SLO): prefer same-region adapters with sufficient headroom, fallback chain: same-region spare pool -> different-region warm pool -> lower-cost low-latency quantized variant.
- Cost first (cost SLO): prefer low-cost adapters or batched endpoints; can increase latency.
- Compliance/region-affinity: tenant-level constraint to never route outside specified region.
- Redundancy: multi-adapter route with primary + fallback endpoints and configurable quick-fail thresholds.

Policy evaluation model
- Orchestrator holds policy graph. Gateway queries orchestrator with request meta (tenant, path, hints). Orchestrator returns route decision with TTL. Gateway caches route decisions locally for TTL.
- For high-throughput, gateways can keep a short-lived local evaluator for simple policies (weights, region-affinity) precompiled from orchestrator pushes. Complex policy evaluation remains on orchestrator.

Multi-region control plane approach
- Pattern: control plane is logically global, physically region-redundant. Use region replicas in 3 regions. Elect a single leader for git-reconciler via small lease (patroni/raft style or cloud leader election). Leader computes authoritative policy deltas and pushes signed snapshots to replicas and gateways.
- Config propagation: changes are git commits -> reconciler -> signer -> push to distribution bus (pub/sub) -> gateway/adapters pull. Use signed manifests to avoid stale/untrusted configs.
- Failure modes: region-replica loss -> fallback to nearest replica; in leader loss, quick leader election with bounded convergence time (target < 30s).

Ownership map (proposed)
- platform-gateway: owns nginx/edge proxies, auth/lambda plugins, rate-limiter, initial route cache; SLA: 99.95 for request ingress under normal load.
- platform-orchestration: owns policy engine, git reconciler, rollout APIs, route decision API; SLA: 99.9 for route decision API, 5s median on route queries.
- serving-runtime: owns adapter binaries, adapter lifecycle, model-manifest schema v1 compilers, integration tests for adapters; SLA: 99.9 for adapter health per pool.
- platform-routing (cross-functional): owns routing policy definitions, library of policy snippets, and the policy test harness (unit + integration).

Example request flow (happy path)
1) Client -> Gateway (auth + quota check)
2) Gateway cache miss -> Query orchestrator route-eval (tenant + hints)
3) Orchestrator returns route decision -> gateway forwards request to adapter endpoint (or via data-plane passthrough)
4) Adapter serves inference, reports usage/latency back to observability and to orchestrator metrics stream
5) Orchestrator updates weights/rollouts asynchronously based on metrics and signals

Adapter evolution and versioning
- Adapters must support a stable manifest v1. Future changes: v2 with explicit capability negotiation.
- Backwards compatibility: orchestrator must maintain adapter capability table; when new capability required, orchestrator performs canary gating and compatibility checks.

Operational playbooks (short)
- Gateway overload: gateway falls back to cached route decisions, rate-limit at edge, send RIT ticket.
- Orchestrator unresponsive: gateways use cached local precompiled policies for TTL window; if expired, gateway returns 503 with informative header X-RI-Fallback:policy-stale.
- Adapter pool degradation: orchestrator routes to alternative adapters per fallback chain, trigger autoscale for dedicated pools, notify on-call serving-runtime.

Open questions / tradeoffs to track
- How much policy evaluation should live at gateway to avoid orchestrator hot-path? (perf vs. control)
- Signed route decisions: what signing algorithm and key rotation cadence? (KMS integration)
- Failover consistency: do we allow eventual consistency across replicas for policy pushes? what is acceptable TTL?
- Ownership for emergent features like request-level sampling for quality evals — platform-routing or product-hosted-api?

Next steps and immediate work items
- Create JIRA epic JIRA-PLAT-790: implement route-decision signing + pub/sub distribution.
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane-proto pull request to add routeDecision.v1 fields (Aisha).
- Test: add policy fuzz tests to policy-harness (owner: Taylor).
- Workshop: 2-hour cross-team session to align on SLA numbers and adapter manifest fields (invite list: gateway, orchestration, serving-runtime, platform-routing).

Appendix: quick sketch of messages (textual)
- RouteEvalRequest { tenantId, path, sessionHints, latencyBudgetMs }
- RouteDecision { routeId, adapterEndpoint, modelId, signedBy, validUntil }
- AdapterManifest { modelId, artifactHash, capabilities:[batching,kv-cache,quantized], sizeMb }

Notes to reviewers
- This is a proposal. Looking for feedback on: degree of logic at gateway vs orchestrator, list of adapter types, and the signed route decision approach.
- Please leave comments inline or add to linked confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234.
